messages:
jamie_cs: FYI customer 'Acme Corp' hit a weird provisioning edge-case after an Okta account merge — they say deprovisioned users still retain org roles in the Console. Reported while troubleshooting an audit; they did an Okta merge (secondary -> primary), then deleted the merged account. SCIM logs show the delete/patch calls returned 200 but roles were not removed on our side.

mike_eng: Can you paste the SCIM payloads / logs (redacted) and the user externalId(s)? suspect some externalId mismatch after the merge. Also which role(s) are sticking?

jamie_cs: Pasting sanitized excerpts from the customer's SCIM log (redacted externalIds/emails):

```
PATCH /scim/v2/Users/281 HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/scim+json
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],
  "Operations": [
    {"op":"replace","path":"active","value":false}
  ]
}
----
DELETE /scim/v2/Users/281 HTTP/1.1 200 OK
okta-bot: SCIM event: user.externalId changed: 0a1b2c -> 9f8e7d (merge), followed by delete for user id 281
```

jamie_cs: They also provided a Console screenshot showing the user still in the "Engineering" org role after the delete. Customer is worried this leaves privileged access available despite deprovision.

mike_eng: Thanks. Initial theory: our deprovision path currently resolves role mappings by externalId -> membership records. If Okta did a merge and assigned a new externalId, the delete may be for the old user id or the new one depending on order, leaving the mapping dangling. We also have a caching layer in role-mapper that keys off externalId hash; if we don't invalidate both old and new keys we can end up with orphaned role entries.

sam_support: Repro steps request: 1) create two Okta users (A and B) with different externalIds, 2) assign group->role mapping to A via SCIM, 3) merge A into B (Okta externalId switch), 4) trigger SCIM delete for A or patch active:false for A. Did customer do merge-then-delete or delete-then-merge? That ordering matters.

jamie_cs: They said merge happened first, then admin deleted the old (secondary) account. So delete came after merge.

mike_eng: Short-term mitigation: run a repair job that does these steps for Acme tenant: 1) scan role_mappings table for entries with stale externalIds reported in Okta audit 2) cross-check against Console users by primaryEmail and userName 3) drop mappings for users not present in Okta or mark as tombstoned and emit audit event. I can run the repair once we get approval.

mike_eng: Long-term fix options (proposal):
- deprovision flow: when resolving mapping, attempt lookup by externalId, then by primaryEmail, then by userName before deciding to skip.
- make role-mapper cache key a composite (externalId|email) and invalidate both sides on merge events.
- emit a deprovision-warning if externalId lookup fails but email lookup succeeds (so CS gets alerted).

marie_se: +1 on audit events. Also recommend we add a telemetry metric for "orphaned-role-detection" so we can alert larger tenants automatically. Need to check compliance implications for auto-removal.

sam_support: Operational question: do we have permission to run the repair for Acme? we need their written approval and a change window since it modifies role_mappings.

jamie_cs: I'll ask Acme for approval and schedule during their maintenance window. They want root cause and ETA first. Can you estimate time for bug + repair?

mike_eng: Bug + PR for fallback lookup + tests: ~2-3d. Repair script + one-time run + verification: ~1 day. If we triage higher we can do a hotfix for repair first, then follow-up for code changes. I'll open a ticket and link here.

sam_support: Also flag support runbook so CS can advise other tenants that report similar symptoms.

jamie_cs: Thanks — I'll update Acme and get the approval note. tagging @mike_eng for follow-up once I have signed consent. :eyes:
